newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican pension fund firms to tighten belts on VAT.
newsitem.headline: Mexican pension fund firms to tighten belts on VAT.

text.p: Mexico's fledgling private pension fund management firms (Afores) on Wednesday welcomed a law that spares workers from paying value added tax on commissions paid to the firms.
But they said the move may hurt the companies' bottom lines.

"The decision is an excellent measure for the system and the workers, and it should further stimulate people to sign up," Ralf Peters Castilla, head of the Mexican Afore Association, the industry lobbying group, told Reuters.
On Wednesday, the Chamber of Deputies overwhelmingly approved modifications to the VAT law to exempt worker contributions to Afores, which would start to be paid in July.
Currently, the 17 Afores are on a publicity drive to sign up workers, but the response has been lukewarm because of the high commissions the pension firms sought to charge.
Peters noted, however, that the exemption will mean the Afores will have to pay the VAT, which he said would raise costs and crimp earnings.
"We're in talks with the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) and with the Finance Ministry to find mechanisms that help us to cut costs," he said.

Currently, one of the heaviest burdens on Afores is the cost of issuing new social security credentials, and the pension firms are seeking to cut those costs in half at a meeting scheduled with the IMSS next week.
Peters, who also heads market leader Afore Bancomer, said his own firm may also reduce publicity expenditures.
Of 10 million dollars in advertising costs budgeted for 1997, Afore Bancomer has already spent $7 million, he said.
-- Cyntia Barrera Diaz, Mexico City newsroom, +525 728-9549
